allometry.note: About 0.6 m tall at 4 years in the open, by eye within the heights floras and guides give (11 to 130 cm in the Flora of North America; commonly 15 to 70 cm), as search results quote them. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaves and stem; waxy white to cream flowers (PNW Flowers and Minnesota Wildflowers, as search results quote them: white or very pale cream; the only western Platanthera that is not yellowish or greenish); pale green buds and green capsules.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its spike drawn as one cluster that opens by the day (spec rework L1c), its kind and flowers from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; each flower about 1.2 cm across, set by hand within the 6 to 13 mm the characters give; slender green capsules after. The plant stands as tall as before: its stem ends where the spike begins.

appearance.organs.flower.season.note: Its days by eye. No flora gives months for the Pacific Northwest (PNW Flowers: mid-summer); dated photographs in E-Flora BC run from June 6 to July 25, and floras elsewhere give June to September. So buds in mid-June, flowers from early July, each open about 12 days, the spike opening from its foot over about 25 days, capsules split by late August and shed by early October; an inference, not a flora's dates.

appearance.organs.flower.season.flower_l.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): three sepals and three petals, the median petal the lip, turned half round so the lip hangs below, on an inferior ovary with a column, and a spurred lip, all from the characters of the Orchidaceae and the species by the rules at the flowering plants. By hand, from the Flora of North America as portals quote it and the Wisconsin orchid pages, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): the lip about 1.3 times a petal's length (lip 4 to 11 mm, petals 3 to 8 mm), the sepals about as long as the petals (3 to 9 mm), all lanceolate and pointed; the dilated base of the lip is not drawn.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from descriptions in floras and field guides, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): one straight, slender, leafy stem from a fleshy rootstock; about five lanceolate leaves scattered up its lower part, the longest about 18 cm (the Flora of North America gives 3.5 to 32 cm), ascending and smaller upward, the top ones bract-like; the spike above them about 18 cm long (1 to 3 dm). A plant flowers from its third year, by eye; floras give no age. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

generator.spreads.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for spec rework P5 as the library's first orchid, from floras and field guides as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read). Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
